content:
Meta announced that parents can now receive notifications when their children discuss suicide or other self-harm behaviors through its artificial intelligence (AI) on Instagram, Facebook, or Meta Horizons.

You need to first enable Meta's parental supervision tools before you can select which children's accounts to monitor……

Meta stated that the new features are a supplement to existing safety measures.

The company said the goal is to detect even fairly veiled references, but all flagged conversations will be reviewed manually.

If you have not yet set up family supervision features for your child's account, please complete the setup first. The new features are currently rolling out in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia.

Meta currently issues alerts to emergency services when credible suicide risks are detected in Facebook or Instagram posts, and stated that this will be expanded to Meta AI in the future.

If you yourself feel at risk, you can call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, or visit 988lifeline.org for an online chat. You may also call 911 or go to the emergency room to request assistance with a mental health emergency.
